To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

locally normalized filter bank features, which are based on a new approach to the development of dynamic features, are significantly more effective than Mel filter bank features for robust speech recognition.

the use of the LNFB coefficients, which are based on locally normalized power spectral density estimates, provides a significant improvement in robust speech recognition accuracy over the use of MFCCs.
locally normalized filter banks, when used with a DNN-HMM system, can improve the performance on the Aurora4 task by 11.4%.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a novel feature extraction method that can be used in conjunction with a robust speech recognition system to improve the recognition accuracy in noisy environments.
the development of a robust front-end for DNN-based speech recognition systems.
the design of robust acoustic features for DNN-HMM-based speech recognition systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the LNFB features provide the best performance of all the filter banks tested, including the widely used Mel filter bank, and that they provide the best performance for the task of Aurora-4 robustness evaluation.

, for the Aurora-2 and Aurora-4 tasks, the use of the proposed features in conjunction with the DNN-HMM-based recognition system results in a substantial reduction in the error rate, and that this reduction is more significant than the error-rate reduction obtained using the MFCC-derived features.
the proposed method is a promising technique for improving robustness of DNN-HMM-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed features are a very effective alternative to MFCC-derived features for robust speech recognition.
the proposed method is more robust to the mismatch between training and testing conditions, and more effective in dealing channel diversity.

the use of the proposed LNFB features in conjunction with DNNs can improve the robustness of a speech recognition system to noise and channel mismatch, which is a significant contribution to the field of robust speech recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the proposed features are robust to channel mismaches, which is an essential property for a feature set to be used in real world applications, and are competitive with state of the art features in clean conditions.
the use of the LNFB coefficients, which are derived from a locally normalizing transform, is more effective in robust speech recognition than the use of MFCCs.
LNCC features, which are derived using a different approach than MFCC features, are better suited for use in DNN-HMM-based systems than MFCC features.
